newsitem.title: USA: USDA declares Medfly emergency in Florida.
newsitem.headline: USDA declares Medfly emergency in Florida.

text.p: Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman on Thursday declared an emergency outbreak of the Mediterranean fruit fly in Florida, threatening citrus, fruit and vegetable crops.
The declaration gives the USDA access to emergency funds to help pay for the $2.1 million eradication programme.

The Medfly, known to scientists as Ceratitis capitata, is one of the most destructive pests of over 200 species of fruits, nuts, and vegetables, especially citrus and stone fruits, Glickman said in a Federal Register notice.

The pest can spread easily, causing severe damage to entire citrus and other fruit and vegetable growing areas. At least 43 countries are known to regulate in some manner for the Mediterranean fruit fly.
An infestation of the pest was found earlier this month in a portion of Florida's Hillsborough County, near Tampa.
"The presence of this fruit fly in the continental United States could severely disrupt the fruit and vegetable industry due to the loss of export markets," Glickman said in his declaration.

Florida's agricultural industry, worth an estimated $6 billion annually, is based on continued trade in international markets. Last year the state produced citrus fruits and juice valued at about $940 million.
